claims.text: SPS at approximately 1800–1900 °C under high uniaxial pressure and optimized pulsed DC conditions will fully densify ZrB2.
ZrB2 produced by the proposed SPS process will remain single-phase.
The proposed SPS process will enhance the structural integrity of ZrB2.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will be less susceptible to pore formation and degradation during long-term liquid-plating-bath exposure.
Conventional ZrB2 requires sintering above 2300 °C.
Conventionally sintered ZrB2 typically has residual porosity.
Conventionally sintered ZrB2 typically has a nonuniform and grain-coarsened microstructure.
Residual porosity and microstructural nonuniformity reduce the strength of conventional ZrB2.
Residual porosity and microstructural nonuniformity increase the susceptibility of ZrB2 to corrosion during liquid-plating exposure.
Pressure-assisted SPS enhances neck formation and rapid densification in ZrB2.
Rapid SPS processing minimizes grain growth and porosity in ZrB2.
SPS reduces prolonged processing exposure relative to a conventional preparation technique.
High heating rates, localized Joule heating, and applied pressure during SPS accelerate diffusion in ZrB2.
High heating rates, localized Joule heating, and applied pressure during SPS accelerate ZrB2 particle bonding.
Rapid densification lowers the temperature required to form fully dense, single-phase ZrB2.
Limiting pore development produces a more uniform and mechanically robust ZrB2 microstructure.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will have higher mechanical strength than ZrB2 conventionally sintered above 2300 °C.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will have greater resistance to corrosive attack and hole formation than conventionally sintered ZrB2 during prolonged liquid-plating-bath exposure.
SPS is known to lower ceramic sintering temperatures and improve densification.
The proposed SPS process may introduce thermal gradients or residual stresses that impede complete single-phase formation.
